dedupe_keys.name: texas february 2021 winter storm uri blackout and cascading failures

description: This case study covers the February 2021 Texas freeze, during which Winter Storm Uri caused generator and gas supply failures that forced grid operator ERCOT to shed load, leaving more than 4.5 million customers, over 10 million people, without power at the peak, some for several days. Busby and co-authors trace how about 30 GW of generation outages and feedback between electricity and gas failures cascaded into drinking water treatment and medical services, with losses estimated at 130 billion dollars in Texas, attribute the depth of the crisis to a failure to winterise after 2011, and point to weatherisation, demand response and interstate interconnection as remedies. Potts and co-authors add 14 interviews with Texas electric utilities, recommending sectionalised circuits for load shed, mutual aid and social media outreach. The papers were published in 2021 and 2024 and are available free under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 and CC BY 4.0 licences respectively. Caveats: loss figures are estimates cited by the authors and the interview study covers only utilities. It informs cascading failure modelling and cold-weather resilience planning for coupled energy and water systems; a related record is the Cascading Failure Resilience Index model.
